10.title: Rollback warning
10.about: The server returned less than this device had already seen (here, an update was deleted from the database).

11.title: Admin dashboard
11.about: The read-only dashboard on the loopback-only admin port (desktop only): accounts, storage, private and shared notes, history versions, live connections, activity per day and API health. Metadata only: nothing in it can be decrypted.

12.title: Recently deleted
12.about: Delete moves a note to “Recently deleted”, with an Undo for a few seconds. It's above the notes in the sidebar, with the count beside it: from there a note can be restored, or deleted forever, which removes it from the server. After 30 days it goes by itself.

13.title: Share a note
13.about: Share above the open note (the share icon; or a right-click on it in the list → Share…) creates two links, one to edit and one to view. The key is in the link, after the #, so the note stays end-to-end encrypted. The list marks shared notes, and the Share icon gets a dot: green while others' edits arrive live, grey while it reconnects.

16.title: History
16.about: The clock button above a note opens its history: earlier versions, by day, kept at most every hour while it's edited (for a year, thinning out as they age). Each row counts the lines it added and removed; Now on top is the note as it is. Pick one to see what it changed since the version before (Changes, unchanged lines folded) or the whole of it (Text); Restore this version makes the note read like that again, as one edit (with an Undo, and the note as it was kept as a version too).

17.title: Formatting
17.about: Notes are markdown, drawn formatted: headings, bold, links, quotes and code, bullets, and checkboxes for tasks (a tick is an ordinary edit, so it syncs and can be undone). The marks are hidden except on the line you're editing (here, the "tram 28" task). Settings → Editor chooses this (Live preview), Show marks (formatted, the marks faint) or Plain text, on every device; ⋮ → Show markdown shows one note's markdown for a moment. A click in a link shows a card with its real address (its text can say otherwise), to open or copy; Ctrl/Cmd+click opens it at once. The text itself doesn't change: the list shows this note as "Trip to Lisbon", without the #.

18.title: When something's wrong
18.about: The app says what happened, with a way out, instead of going blank. A page left open across an update offers to reload (here, the server's answers were made to name another version). A note that fails to open says why, where it would be; the others still open. If the app's scripts don't load or fail as it starts, the page says so (here, one module was blocked), with the error. Edits waiting to upload are kept on the device in every case.

01.title: Create a vault
01.about: A new vault is just a passkey. Plim makes the 12 words behind it, and reminds you to save them until you have. (Without a passkey, the 12 words are shown and confirmed instead: see A passkey without PRF.)

02.title: Sign in on another device
02.about: Where the passkey syncs, it signs in by itself. Anywhere else, the 12 words open the same vault, and Plim offers to add a passkey there.

03.title: Notes
03.about: On a phone, the list and the open note are separate screens. Above the note: its title, then History (a point on a timeline), Share, and ⋮ (Show markdown, Delete note). A right-click on a note in the list (a long press on a phone) gives Share… and Delete note without opening it. Above the notes: New note, which stays put, and Recently deleted (with its count), which scrolls with the list; the list shows the 30 most recent notes and then Show all. On desktop the sidebar can be hidden (the panel button at its top, or Ctrl+\), and is kept so in that browser; then the same button at the left of the note's bar, or pointing at the window's left edge, slides it in over the note to pick another, and clicking the button keeps it open again. At the bottom: your menu (Settings, and below a line Log out, which locks this device; each with its icon). On a phone, New note is at the bottom instead, to the right of your menu; and the note's bar is a chevron back to the list, the title centred, and one ⋯ holding who's here, History, Share (with its state: Live or Reconnecting), Show markdown and Delete note. The sharing light is on the ⋯, and others in the note show as their initials. Every edit is saved as you type; the app only says something about saving when there's a problem (storage full, a note too large, or a save that keeps failing).

04.title: Lock and unlock
04.about: Log out in your menu (bottom left) locks this device: your notes stay saved on it, and a device that has used a passkey opens on “Welcome back”. The 12 words always work too.

05.title: Settings
05.about: In sections: Profile (your name, for shared notes), Editor (how notes' markdown is drawn, and the shortcuts: see Formatting), Sign-in & security (passkeys, the 12 words and changing them, auto-lock), Storage and Account (the account ID, and deleting the account). On a desktop the sections are listed beside the chosen one; on a phone it opens on the list, and a section opens on its own with ← Settings.

06.title: Change the recovery phrase
06.about: A new phrase re-encrypts everything under a new key. The old phrase and every passkey’s copy of it stop working everywhere; this device can keep its passkey with one more prompt.

07.title: Forget this device
07.about: “Forget this device” (after the browser’s confirmation) removes the offline copies and brings back “Create a new vault”. The passkeys keep working.

08.title: Offline
08.about: With the server unreachable, the app still opens, unlocks from the device’s saved copy, and keeps edits until it’s back.

09.title: A passkey without PRF
09.about: Passkey sign-in needs the WebAuthn PRF extension. When a password manager doesn’t provide it, Plim says so, and the vault is created with the 12 words instead.
